text: Order these couplings from weakest to strongest: a `new` call on a collaborator, a `List` parameter, shared mutable static state, extending a class.
choices: `new` call, `List` parameter, shared mutable static state, extending a class.
`List` parameter, `new` call, extending a class, shared mutable static state.
`List` parameter, extending a class, `new` call, shared mutable static state.
Extending a class, `new` call, `List` parameter, shared mutable static state.
explanation: A parameter is data coupling, the weakest. A `new` call adds knowledge of how to build the collaborator, which is why moving it to the caller — dependency injection — removes half of it. Inheritance is stronger still, since you depend on internal calls nobody documented. Shared mutable static state is worst: everything touching it is coupled to everything else touching it, invisibly, and Chapter 31 shows what that does when threads arrive.
